title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page. M is a 1-dimensional 'multiplicité', i.e. a smooth Deligne–Mumford curve stack or orbifold curve, quasi-projective over a field k. Grothendieck assumes that M has a finite étale Galois cover U → M, with group G, such that U is a scheme; U is then a smooth quasi-projective curve. He takes k of characteristic 0.

Case k algebraically closed. There is the extension (11): 1 → Π0 = π1(U) → Π = π1(M,a) → G → 1. Π0 is the fundamental group of a punctured curve and carries its natural 'L-structure'. By the Longue Marche terminology ('groupes/groupoïdes à lacets'), L most plausibly refers to the conjugacy classes of 'lacets': loops around the punctures, i.e. the inertia generators, possibly with orientation data. This structure is transported to Π. The page asserts that the resulting L-structure on Π does not depend on the choice of the Galois cover U, nor on the chosen lift of the geometric base point a to U. Π is from now on tacitly equipped with it.

Case k arbitrary. Grothendieck singles out k of finite type over Q as the most interesting case. The homotopy exact sequence (12) reads 1 → π1(M_k̄,a) → π1(M,a) → Γ_{k̄/k} → 1. The geometric fundamental group inherits an L-structure from π, so π appears as an arithmetic extension of Γ by an L-group, i.e. an 'L-group over Γ'. The Galois action respects the loop/inertia classes.

Grothendieck then says he is mainly interested in the 'universal' case of type (g,ν). There the base is not Spec k but the modular multiplicity M_{g,ν}. This leads, on the next page, to the remark that moduli of curves with a prescribed discrete L-group type form a 2-category fibered in groupoids (a 2-stack), not merely a fibered category.

Purpose. The aim is to set up the anabelian/Teichmüller-tower formalism (Longue Marche) for orbifold curves, with fundamental groups carrying cusp/loop data and a Galois action.
errors: The assumption on the previous page ('il doit être vrai') that every 1-dimensional multiplicity admits a finite étale Galois cover by a scheme is false in general. The 'bad' orbifolds are counterexamples: P^1 with a single cone point (teardrop), or two cone points of different orders (spindle). These have no manifold, hence no scheme, finite étale cover. The claim holds for good orbifold curves, in particular all hyperbolic types and anything with enough punctures. Grothendieck explicitly flags it as a supposition.

Sequence (12) is exact as written only if M is geometrically connected over k. Characteristic 0 (or tameness) is needed for the transported loop/inertia structure to behave well; char 0 was assumed on the previous page.

The independence of the L-structure from the choice of U and of base-point lifts is asserted ('manifestement'), not proved. It is plausible: covers can be dominated by a common cover, and inner automorphisms preserve conjugacy classes of loops.

ideas.what: Étale fundamental group of a DM curve stack (multiplicité) via a finite étale scheme cover, as an extension of the Galois group G by π1(U)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Noohi (2004), Zoonekynd; orbifold π1 of Thurston in topology
ideas.where_published: Multiplicités modulaires appear in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Canonical L-structure (loop/inertia conjugacy classes) on π1 of an orbifold curve, transported from a scheme cover and independent of choices
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal/inertia structure on the fundamental group of a hyperbolic orbicurve
ideas.where_published: Groupes à lacets in La Longue Marche (1981); this continuation is unpublished

ideas.what: Homotopy exact sequence over a field of finite type over Q, with induced L-structure making π an arithmetic L-group over Γ
ideas.modern_name: outer Galois representation on the fundamental group preserving inertia classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: SGA1 (exact sequence); Ihara, Deligne, Nakamura (inertia preservation)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 Exp. IX–X for the exact sequence; Esquisse d'un programme for the anabelian context

ideas.what: Passage to the universal family of type (g,ν) over the modular stack M_{g,ν}, and (next page) moduli of a given L-group type forming a 2-stack
ideas.modern_name: relative fundamental groups over moduli stacks; gerbes/2-stacks of curves with level structure

missed.claim: A programme to build moduli multiplicities attached to a discrete L-group 'type' over Q or Z. Grothendieck recognises that these naturally form a 2-stack rather than a stack. The idea starts on this page and continues on the next; no construction is given.
missed.quote: Je suis particulièrement intéressé au cas "universel" du type (g, ν) — mais la base n'est pas alors le [Spectre d'un corps]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is related to moduli of curves with G-structures and to Teichmüller-type stacks with profinite or discrete group data. The 2-stack phenomenon is now standard (gerbes), so its novelty is limited.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful setup of stacky fundamental groups with loop (inertia) structure and their Galois action. It is coherent and consistent with La Longue Marche, but the content is now standard: orbifold π1, homotopy exact sequence, inertia-preserving Galois action. The only mild interest is the early recognition of 2-stack moduli, which belongs to the next page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'dépend pas du choix des rev. étales {+finis+} galoisiens' is right; 'finis' is inserted above 'galoisiens'.
'comme un Π-groupe [?]' is doubtful. The image shows something like 'TL-groupe' with a stroke, most likely 'L-groupe' or a Γ-indexed L-groupe (an L-group over Γ_{k̄/k}), not 'Π-groupe'.
'tacitement' is an insertion above 'tjrs'; reading: 'Nous munirons tacitement tjrs π = π1(M,a) de cette L-structure.'
'(le cas le plus intéressant étant celui où k est ext. de type fini de Q)' is consistent with the image.
